title: Building permit in rural Morocco: 1 ha rule, douars, exemptions
h1: Building permit in rural Morocco: rules, exemptions and procedure
desc: Building outside urban areas in Morocco: the 1-hectare rule, 1/50 footprint, 8.50 m height, delimited douars, farmland, architect and procedure.
intro: Building in the countryside is not a free-for-all: depending on where your plot lies, a building permit is mandatory and minimum rules apply. Here is what the legal texts say, and what has changed for douars (rural villages).
body:
In short: in rural areas, a building permit (permis de construire) is mandatory within urban perimeters and their peripheral zones, in rural settlements covered by a development plan, in authorised subdivisions, within 1 km of the centre line of a non-municipal road or a railway, and within 5 km of the coast (art. 40 of Law 12-90). Where no zoning plan applies, the baseline rule is a plot of at least 1 hectare, a building footprint limited to 1/50 of the plot (800 m² maximum) and a height of 8.50 m (Decree No. 2-92-832, art. 34). Exemptions exist, notably in douars delimited since the joint circular of April 2023.

Where is a building permit mandatory in rural Morocco?

Law 12-90 on urban planning (loi relative à l'urbanisme), in the consolidated version published by the General Secretariat of the Government (Secrétariat général du gouvernement, October 2024), prohibits building without a permit:

  • in urban municipalities (communes urbaines), delimited centres (centres délimités) and their peripheral zones (up to 15 km around cities, art. 1), as well as in special-purpose zones (zones à vocation spécifique);
  • outside those perimeters and outside rural settlements covered by a development plan: along railways and roads other than municipal roads, within 1 km of their centre line, and along the maritime public domain within 5 km;
  • in authorised subdivisions (lotissements autorisés), wherever they are located.

In a rural settlement covered by an approved rural development plan (plan de développement des agglomérations rurales, PDAR), prior authorisation is required by Dahir No. 1-60-063 of 25 June 1960. In practice, almost every "saleable" plot falls into one of these cases: check before you buy.

Which rules apply if no zoning plan covers the plot?

Article 46 of Law 12-90 refers to regulatory standards (minimum plot size, buildable area, height) and itself sets the setbacks. These standards are laid down by Decree No. 2-92-832 of 14 October 1993 implementing Law 12-90 (art. 34 to 37, Official Bulletin No. 4225); Circular No. 65/DGUAAT/DUA/SJ of 30 March 1994 is only an implementation commentary and is not legally binding as such:

RuleValueLegal text
Minimum plot size1 hectare (10,000 m²)Decree 2-92-832, art. 34
Buildable footprint1/50 of the plot, 800 m² maximumDecree 2-92-832, art. 34
Maximum height8.50 m, including all rooftop structuresDecree 2-92-832, art. 34
Setback from the public road10 m from the right-of-way boundaryLaw 12-90, art. 46
Setback from neighbours5 m from the boundary linesLaw 12-90, art. 46
Water and sanitationConnection required, unless exempted after a health opinionLaw 12-90, art. 47

Example: on a 1 ha plot, the footprint is capped at 200 m² (10,000 ÷ 50). A two-storey house (R+1) can therefore offer around 400 m² of floor area if the height stays below 8.50 m. If the plot comes from an authorised subdivision, its specifications (cahier des charges) and plans apply instead.

Can you build on less than one hectare?

Yes, in two regulated cases:

  1. Individual exemption (dérogation): Article 35 of Decree No. 2-92-832 allows a permit to be granted on a smaller plot, because of the state of land division, after a binding opinion (avis conforme) from an administrative committee, provided the project does not encourage scattered development. Article 36 allows the footprint or height limits to be exceeded, after an opinion from the same committee, where the technical nature of the building requires it (sheds, agro-industrial units, places of worship…). Article 37 sets the committee's composition (in particular the planning, public works, agriculture and housing departments). Circular 65 of 1994 comments on these exemptions.
  2. Delimited douars: an administrative instruction (not a regulatory text), the joint circular of the Ministries of Urban Planning and of the Interior dated 28 April 2023, entrusts a provincial committee, under the authority of the wali or governor, with delimiting douars not covered by a planning document. Within these perimeters, residents can obtain a permit even below the one-hectare threshold, provided the building does not encourage scattered housing. In June 2026 the press reported, citing the ministry, that the number of delimited douars had risen from 975 to 4,698.

Ask the municipality (commune) or the Urban Agency (agence urbaine) whether your douar is delimited: this is often what unlocks a small family plot.

Can you build on agricultural land?

Land classified as agricultural is not freely buildable. Outside any zoning plan, the rules in the table apply (1 ha, 1/50, 8.50 m). If a zoning plan (plan d'aménagement) or a PDAR covers the land, its zoning decides: the zoning information certificate (note de renseignements urbanistiques) will tell you. Agricultural land cannot be carved into building lots either: outside urban perimeters, Law 25-90 (art. 9) only allows a subdivision for scattered housing, tourism or agriculture, with lots of at least one hectare; this article is among those amended by Law No. 34-21 (Official Bulletin No. 7533 of 10 August 2026): have its new wording checked. Beware of sales of undivided "shares" (indivision) presented as buildable lots.

Is an architect mandatory in rural areas?

It depends on the location:

  • In urban municipalities, delimited centres, their peripheral zones and special-purpose zones, an architect registered with the Order of Architects (Ordre des architectes) is mandatory for any new building (art. 50). For 150 m² of floor area or less, the architect's mandatory assignment is limited to design (art. 54).
  • Outside these perimeters, an architect is only required for public buildings or buildings open to the public (art. 51). For a private house, the law does not require one. The drawings must still pass the review, and the architectural assistance offered in douars does not cover every case.

Using an architect remains the safest way to get through the review committee first time and to comply with earthquake-resistance (seismic) rules. See our guide to architect fees in Morocco.

What is the step-by-step procedure?

  1. Check the status of the land: land title (titre foncier) or legal status, applicable planning document, delimited douar or not. Request a zoning information certificate (note de renseignements urbanistiques).
  2. Have the project designed in line with the applicable rules: location plan, floor plans, elevations, sanitation method if there is no sewer network.
  3. File the application with the municipality, increasingly through the Rokhas platform (see our Rokhas guide). The general building regulations (règlement général de construction, Decree 2-18-577) classify as "major projects" (grands projets) buildings outside a subdivision whose land has no use assigned by a zoning, land-use or development plan: the review committee then brings together the municipality, the Urban Agency and the relevant departments.
  4. Wait for the decision: if the president of the municipal council does not respond, the permit is deemed granted two months after filing (art. 48). For major projects, the category covering buildings outside a planning document, Joint Order No. 1839-23 (Official Bulletin No. 7212, July 2023) sets an overall time limit of 30 days between the filing receipt and issue (15 days for small projects). The permit lapses if foundations have not started within one year (art. 49).
  5. Pay the taxes when collecting the permit: see our guide to building permit fees and taxes. The exemption for "rural-type dwellings located in rural municipalities" is in Article 52 of Law 47-06: have it confirmed that it applies to your house.
  6. Build, then apply for the occupancy permit (permis d'habiter).

What about the province of Kénitra?

Applications there are reviewed with the Urban Agency of Kénitra-Sidi Kacem-Sidi Slimane (Agence urbaine de Kénitra-Sidi Kacem-Sidi Slimane). Several rural centres have their own zoning plan or PDAR, such as Sidi Allal Tazi, Lalla Mimouna or Arbaoua: the 1 ha rule does not apply there as such. Law 64-23, published in the Official Bulletin of 10 August 2026, creates regional urban planning and housing agencies (agences régionales de l'urbanisme et de l'habitat) that gradually replace the urban agencies as each one is actually set up (agency by agency). Check which office is competent when you file. See also our page architect in Kénitra and the guide to the Kénitra zoning plan.

How much does a house cost in a rural area?

Construction cost depends mainly on floor area, the site and the finishes, not on rural status. For a first estimate, use our free estimating tool and the guide to construction cost per m². Still looking for land? Browse our land listings, always checking the zoning information certificate. Arabic version of this guide: رخصة البناء في العالم القروي. For the general framework, read our guide to the building permit in Morocco.

An architect registered with the Order can check your plot and the rule that applies to it, then put the application together with you. The CITURBAREA practice, based in Kénitra, works across the Rabat-Salé-Kénitra region.
faq: Do I need a building permit for a country house in Morocco?

Yes, in the vast majority of cases: in urban municipalities and their peripheral zones, delimited centres, rural settlements covered by a development plan, authorised subdivisions, within 1 km of the centre line of a non-municipal road or a railway, and within 5 km of the coast (art. 40 of Law 12-90). Outside these zones, check with the municipality (commune) before any work.
What is the minimum plot size to build in a rural area?

Outside any zoning plan and outside a subdivision, the baseline rule is one hectare, with a footprint limited to 1/50 of the plot (800 m² maximum) and a height of 8.50 m (Decree No. 2-92-832, art. 34; Circular 65 of 30 March 1994 comments on its application). Exemptions exist after a binding opinion from a committee (art. 35 to 37 of the decree), and douars delimited since the circular of 28 April 2023 allow building below this threshold.

Delimitation is carried out by a provincial committee under the authority of the wali or governor. The rural municipality and the competent Urban Agency (agence urbaine) can tell you whether your douar is included and which rules apply there.
Can I build on agricultural land?

Not freely. If a zoning plan or a development plan covers the land, its zoning decides. Otherwise, the minimum rules apply: one hectare, 1/50 footprint, 8.50 m height. A zoning information certificate (note de renseignements urbanistiques) lets you check this before buying.
Is an architect mandatory to build in a rural area?

An architect is mandatory in urban municipalities, delimited centres, their peripheral zones and special-purpose zones (art. 50 of Law 12-90). Elsewhere, one is only required for public buildings or buildings open to the public (art. 51), but remains strongly recommended to get through the review and comply with seismic rules.
How long does it take to get a permit in a rural area?

The law provides that if the president of the municipal council does not respond, the permit is deemed granted two months after filing (art. 48 of Law 12-90). Joint Order No. 1839-23 (2023) sets an overall time limit of 30 days for major projects, the category covering buildings outside a planning document, and 15 days for small projects. In practice, the time depends on how complete the file is and on the opinions required, especially for projects classed as major projects.
Is the construction tax payable for a rural house?

Article 52 of Law 47-06 exempts rural-type dwellings located in rural municipalities. Whether your project qualifies is for the municipality to decide: have it confirmed by the municipal tax collector (régisseur communal) before collecting the permit.
